rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE AS OF JUNE 30 2011`, PDF pages 76 and 77 of the FY2011 annual town report (4117-fy-2011-annual-town-report.pdf), printed folios 73 and 74. BOTH PAGES ARE PHOTOGRAPHS printed 180 degrees from upright -- pdfplumber returns 0 words on every page of this report. WHY THIS PAGE WAS `refused` AND WHY THAT SAID NOTHING ABOUT THE DOCUMENT: the whole schedule is printed in WHOLE DOLLARS, so the archive's money pattern `[\d,]+\.\d\d` matches 1 of about 300 digit-bearing boxes on p76 and 1 of 79 on p77. A figure the pattern misses is not an absent figure (rule 13c). THE ISSUE IS IDENTIFIED BY ITS PRINTED POSITION, NOT BY ITS NAME. The page prints FOURTEEN issue blocks and only nine distinct names: `MUNICIPAL PURPOSE` appears FIVE times (positions 4, 6, 8, 10 and 14) and `PRINCIPAL`/`INTEREST` repeat under every one of them. Keying on the name collapses five issues into one and overwrites their cells. The position is counted off the page top-down and is asserted unique in the generator. THE TABLE IS RULED -- every cell is boxed -- so unlike the trust matrix on pp.73-74 there is no label-to-figure pairing problem here: a figure is in the year column whose box it sits in. Each issue prints three rows, `PRINCIPAL`, `INTEREST` and a TOTAL row named for the instrument (`TOTAL MASS WATER POLL TRUST` -- the page's own spelling, with POLL for POOL -- or `TOTAL MUNICIPAL PURPOSE`). Years run FY2012-FY2030 on page 76 and FY2031-FY2047 plus a `TOTAL` column on page 77. THIS GROUP is the three summary rows the schedule prints at its foot, `GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL`, `GRAND TOTAL INTEREST` and `TOTAL DEBT`, year by year across both pages. WHAT PROVES IT: the principal row sums across 36 years to the printed $27,097,991 EXACTLY, and 35 of the 36 years close on principal + interest = total debt. AND IT IS CHECKED AGAINST THE DETAIL: for every one of the 36 years the fourteen issues' own figures sum to these printed grand totals -- exactly in all 36 principal columns, and within $1 in four interest columns. THE $1 DIFFERENCES ARE THE DOCUMENT'S, AND THE CONTRAST IS THE EVIDENCE. PRINCIPAL TIES EXACTLY EVERYWHERE: all 14 issue principal totals, all 36 year columns against the printed GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL, and the printed grand total $27,097,991. INTEREST does not: it misses by exactly $1 in 4 of the 36 year columns (+1 in FY2013 and FY2020, -1 in FY2016 and FY2017, netting to zero) and by $1 on MASS WATER POOL 14*'s own total. A MWPAT level-payment loan carries cents and this schedule displays whole dollars, so a printed total is the rounded sum and not the sum of the rounded parts -- THAT IS AN EXPLANATION AND NOT A MEASUREMENT (rule 7). What is measured is the contrast: the column with no cents beneath it closes on 51 separate identities while the column that must carry cents misses by a dollar on five of them. NO TOLERANCE IS DECLARED ANYWHERE IN THIS READING. The misses are ATTESTED, named and reported on every run, which is what a tolerance would have hidden. THE FY2024 CELL THE DOCUMENT LEAVES OUT OF ITS OWN TOTALS. WHAT THE PAGE PRINTS: the issue at position 7, `MASS WATER POOL 9*`, has a FY2024 PRINCIPAL of $418,704 and its FY2024 INTEREST and TOTAL cells are BLANK. GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL for FY2024 is $846,635, which is the sum of the seven issues paying principal that year INCLUDING the $418,704 -- exactly, to the dollar. TOTAL DEBT for FY2024 is $548,241, and $846,635 + $120,310 = $966,945, so the TOTAL DEBT cell is $418,704 LOW; it is GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL plus GRAND TOTAL INTEREST less that one payment. The same exclusion is carried into the TOTAL column: $27,097,991 + $9,263,504 = $36,361,495 against a printed TOTAL DEBT of $35,942,791, short by the same $418,704; and the issue's own printed total, $5,651,592, is the sum of its TWELVE printed year totals (FY2012-FY2023) while its printed principal total $4,580,191 includes the thirteenth year. Every one of those relations closes to the dollar. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: why. A final principal payment with no interest due, a total formula that stopped one column short, and a payment entered in the wrong row all fit the figures identically, and nothing on these two pages distinguishes them. IT IS NOT FY2015'S EXCLUSION. FY2015's printed grand totals leave TWO WHOLE school-construction issues out of every year column ($29.6M of $49.6M). Here one CELL in one year of one issue is missing from two derived rows, and the arithmetic locates it exactly. It DOES match what FY2013 and FY2014 both show -- a `MASS WATER POOL 9*` row with a principal and no interest or total -- so the same issue prints the same way in three consecutive reports. closes: the Treasurer's MWPAT loan amortisation schedule for pool 9, which is not published.

rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG / FY2011 COLLECTION OF TAXES`, PDF page 78 of the FY2011 annual town report (printed folio 75). 49 receivable rows against a printed `GRAND TOTAL`. THE PRINTED COLUMN HEADER, VERBATIM AND IN ORDER (rule 13b.4): `COLLECTION OF TAXES` | `FORWARD` | `COMMITTMENTS` | `ADJUSTMENTS` | `REFUNDS` | `PAYMENTS` | `ABATEMENTS` | `TRANSFER` | `BALANCES`. `COMMITTMENTS` is spelt with two Ts on the page and is recorded as printed, never corrected. WHAT PROVES IT, twice over. (1) ALL EIGHT money columns foot to the printed GRAND TOTAL to the cent with NO tolerance: 1,520,280.74 / 20,901,570.69 / (198,957.22) / 26,258.46 / (20,207,288.18) / (176,592.45) / (284,631.85) / 1,580,640.19. (2) EVERY ONE OF THE 49 ROWS closes on the identity the table states about itself, forward plus committments plus adjustments plus refunds plus payments plus abatements plus transfer equals the balance carried -- declared here as a `row_identity` and re-asserted on every run. THE ROW-TO-FIGURE ALIGNMENT IS FIXED BY ARITHMETIC, NOT BY THE LOOK OF THE PAGE, AND THAT MATTERS HERE MORE THAN ANYWHERE. The scan is sheared: the `BALANCES` column is printed roughly one row pitch BELOW the label it belongs to, and the drift grows left to right, so on the personal-property block the `PAYMENTS` cells appear a row low as well. Read by eye the table would assign 1997 MVE's balance to 1998 MVE and every row after it. Each pairing here was settled by the row identity and then by the eight column totals, which is FY2014 page 42's lesson applied -- an independent total decides an alignment, never the appearance of one. A single mis-assigned row breaks both proofs at once: the columns would still foot (the figures are all present) but 49 row identities would not. SIGNS ARE THE DOCUMENT'S.
